title: A Trail for the Wreck
premise: Dominic Yarrow, a disgraced railroad engineer scraping by on closed-line surveys, pulls a sealed chest from the river and finds inside it a map to the headwaters of the Vell, drawn by an engineer from a nation that no longer exists—and a debt ledger with Dominic's grandfather's name on every page. Hunted by the creditors' syndicate who want the chest's provenance erased, and shadowed by a cartographer's daughter who claims the map as her inheritance, Dominic must travel the forbidden upper river before the monsoon seals the passes. At the source, Dominic discovers the 'dead nation' was buried alive by the very railway it built, and that the chest was left as a message: the debt is real, but so is the proof of what was taken. Dominic chooses to publish the ledger rather than trade it for absolution, ending invisible no longer—alive, exposed, and finally belonging to something larger than survival.
about_author: Paloma Thackeray is a former survey assistant who spent six seasons mapping river corridors across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose livelihoods depend on knowing exactly where the edges of the world are.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up a Secret
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Broke and dodging creditors, Dominic takes a low-paying dredge survey on the lower Vell and hauls up a lead-sealed chest stamped with the extinct nation of Karvel's double-star crest. Inside: a hand-drawn map of the upper river and a ledger of debts. The emotional beat is wary curiosity hardening into dread when Dominic recognizes a family name.

chapters.title: Closed Lines, Open Wounds
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic traces the ledger to a grandfather who engineered Karvel's railways before the nation was 'dissolved'—a euphemism no one explains. The syndicate's first collector arrives, asking polite questions with a knife's patience. The beat: inheritance revealed as something heavier than pride.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ilsa Venn's POV. Ilsa ambushes Dominic in a riverport tavern, claiming the map was her father's life's work and that he died following it. She proposes an uneasy alliance: she reads the terrain, Dominic reads the engineering. The beat is prickly mistrust masking a shared hunger to belong to a finished thing.

chapters.title: Monsoon Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The monsoon's landfall is eleven weeks out; the upper passes close in ten. Dominic and Ilsa buy passage upstream on the barge of a smuggler, Teodor, who charges them in secrets instead of coin. The beat is momentum laced with the first real fear—the syndicate is ahead of them, not behind.

chapters.title: What the Locks Remember
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. At the derelict Karveli lock system, the map's cipher matches carvings on the gates: the 'dead nation' didn't die—it was sealed off when the railway consortium rerouted the river. Teodor reveals he smuggles Karveli survivors' goods. The beat: history stops being abstract and starts having a face.

chapters.title: The Collector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The syndicate's chief collector corners Dominic at a mid-river trading post with an offer: the ledger and map in exchange for full debt forgiveness and a new name. Dominic nearly takes it. The beat is temptation—the price of survival made literal—and the quiet shame of considering it.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ambushed above the trading post, the trio loses the barge and most of their supplies running the Serrano Rapids. Teodor takes a wound that will slow them fatally. The beat is grief and guilt—Dominic's hesitation at the bargain cost them blood—and the alliance fuses into something like family.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the source gorge as the first monsoon squalls hit: a hidden valley where Karveli descendants still live, keeping the locks, waiting for someone to come with the ledger. The chest, they explain, was sent downstream deliberately. The beat is awe collapsing into horror—the debt was engineered to find its heir.

chapters.title: The Weight of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax. The collector arrives with the monsoon at their backs, offering once more to make everything disappear—Karvel, the valley, Dominic's debt. Dominic chooses exposure: reading the ledger aloud at the lock gates, naming every debt and every theft, as the river rises. The beat is terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Wreck
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, resolution. The flood buries the gorge road, but the ledger's copies go out with Teodor's runners before the passes close; the syndicate's silence is now worth more than its knives. Dominic and Ilsa stay through the wet season to survey a new line—one the valley will own. The beat is hard-won belonging: inheritance accepted, price paid, home made.
